text:
sam: hey — bringing up an HF model fork that uses a custom AutoConfig/AutoModel subclass. conversion script bails with a trust_remote_code related error. anyone seen this exact flow?

deploy-bot: conversion-job 78821 started for repo: hf/bigchat-custom (commit: 0a1b2c). log: `ValueError: Unexpected key 'chat_format' in state_dict` -> job failed.

aisha: ping @sam — can you paste the config.json and tokenizer files? often it's an auto_map / special_tokens mismatch. :thinking:

sam: pasted snippets — config.json has `custom_type": "CustomChatConfig"` and there's an `auto_map` entry but it points to a local module `bigchat.configs.chat.CustomChatConfig`. tokenizer only has merges/vocab, no special_tokens_map.json.

kevin: common pattern: HF models that require `trust_remote_code=True` put python classes in their repo. our converter sandbox blocks that by default. converter needs either `--trust-remote-code` or an explicit `auto_map` mapping from hf types -> canonical transformers classes. otherwise it refuses to import arbitrary code.

sam: tried running `redwood-convert --source hf/bigchat-custom --trust-remote-code` and it still errors later: `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'chat_format'` — looks like the CustomChatConfig adds arguments that our runtime's AutoConfig doesn't accept.

aisha: yeah that implies the custom class is changing ctor signature (bad for portability). quick workaround: add an `auto_map` to config.json mapping the custom name to a safe base class, e.g.:

```json
"auto_map": {
  "AutoConfig": "transformers.models.gpt2.configuration_gpt2.GPT2Config",
  "AutoModel": "transformers.models.gpt2.modeling_gpt2.GPT2LMHeadModel",
  "AutoTokenizer": "transformers.models.gpt2.tokenization_gpt2.GPT2Tokenizer"
}
```

That tells the converter to instantiate standard classes and ignore the repo's python. But if the model really depends on custom code (custom attention, chat formatting), that will break behavior.

kevin: also check special tokens — missing `special_tokens_map.json` means `bos_token`/`eos_token` are inferred differently. For chat templates HF uses `chat_format` in config + tokenizer special tokens to build conversation; if those are missing we get garbled prompts during eval. quick fix: create `special_tokens_map.json` with `{"bos_token":"<s>","eos_token":"</s>","pad_token":"<pad>"}` and re-run convert.

sam: added special_tokens_map, reran convert with `--trust-remote-code` again. New error: `RuntimeError: KV cache shape mismatch for layer 5 (expected [batch, heads, seq, head_dim], got [batch, heads, seq-1, head_dim])` — happens only when quantizing to int8.

aisha: that smells like a custom attention implementation that offsets positions or uses rotary embeddings with a different indexing. Quantization can expose small shape assumptions. For now try converting without quant and verify logits/attention shapes first. If that works, run quantization with per-channel vs per-tensor options.

kevin: logging note — we should add a clearer converter error when `trust_remote_code` set but constructor args mismatch. Suggest PR: detect `TypeError` in instantiation and dump constructor signature + config keys difference. Saves a bunch of guesswork.

sam: agreed. immediate plan: 1) revert quant step, get a non-quantized conversion working using `auto_map` fallback for config, 2) add missing special_tokens_map.json, 3) if model still needs custom python for core ops, escalate to eng-runtime to support a safe sandbox `trust_remote_code` path or maintain a small shim that implements the required custom layers in C++/Torch.

aisha: I'll open an RFC and include the conversion log snippets and proposed auto_map heuristics. Kevin — can you prototype the constructor-difference error message?

kevin: on it. will post a small repro + patch later today.

sam: thx. leaving logs here for the PR:

```
ERROR stack:
File "/opt/redwood/bin/redwood-convert", line 212, in <module>
  config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True)
  model = AutoModel.from_config(config)
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'chat_format'
```

sam: also note: model card has a `chat_template.md` that references special tokens `<usr>` and `<sys>` — those must map to tokenizer tokens or prompts will be wrong in evals. added a note to the RFC. :face_with_monocle:
